punchline: Harlan Mills proposed organising programmers like a surgical team: one chief, everyone else in support.
thirty_sec: In 1971 Harlan Mills suggested that a programming team should work like an operating room, and Fred Brooks later described the idea in his book. One chief programmer and a backup do the core work. A clerk keeps the records, a toolsmith builds the tools and a language lawyer knows the language. The chief stays inside the design, and fewer people need to agree on every decision.
